justifications.functional_suitability: Core functional requirements R-01, R-02, and R-04 are thoroughly supported by Search & Discovery, Core E-Commerce Service, and Recommendation Engine. However, customer reviews and 5-star ratings (R-03) are only referenced as data in Amazon DynamoDB without dedicated service or UI components.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Page load under 2s on 3G is enabled by CloudFront CDN, Next.js SSR in BFF Container, and Code-Split Boundary. High throughput for 1M MAU is achieved with Amazon ElastiCache, Amazon MSK event streaming, and Amazon OpenSearch indexing.
justifications.compatibility: Interoperability is fully realized via dedicated integration points: Shipping & Fulfillment Component connects to Third-Party Shipping API, Checkout & Billing Component integrates with Payment Gateway and Tax Calculation Service, and Notification Worker interfaces with external delivery services using REST/HTTPS.
justifications.usability: Customer journeys are supported via Frontend SPA and BFF Container with localized multi-currency support. Admin/Content Manager is provided access through the Frontend SPA and Amazon Athena Query Engine, though specific administrative interfaces or workflows are sparsely detailed.
justifications.reliability: High availability (99.95%) is addressed through multi-region resilience: Route 53 DNS Resolver, CloudFront Origin Groups & Failover, Amazon Aurora Global Database with automated failover, DynamoDB Global Tables, and dead-letter queue handling in Notification Worker.
justifications.security: OWASP mitigations are enforced by AWS WAF and Route Validator & Authorizer. GDPR/CCPA compliance is systematically handled by Consent & Privacy Manager, Security & Compliance Interceptor, and Compliance/Audit Lambda via GDPR/CCPA Data Redactor and Audit Log Ingestor.
justifications.maintainability: The system is decomposed into decoupled services (Search & Discovery, Recommendation Engine, Core E-Commerce Service) communicating via Amazon MSK and gRPC. Minor inconsistency exists between Level 1 and Level 2 container definitions regarding catalog service boundaries.
justifications.portability: Multi-region deployment across us-east-1, eu-west-1, and ap-southeast-1 is well-architected using Route 53, Amazon Aurora Global Database, and DynamoDB Global Tables. However, tight coupling to proprietary AWS services (Athena, Glue, DynamoDB) creates substantial cloud-provider lock-in.

PERF-01.justification: Edge caching via CloudFront, Next.js SSR in the BFF, ElastiCache Redis read replicas with LRU eviction, and DynamoDB DAX provide comprehensive multi-tiered caching to sustain extreme surges while keeping 3G load times under 2 seconds.
sensitivity_points: CloudFront and Redis cache hit ratios
tradeoffs: Aggressive caching may serve slightly stale catalog data during rapid inventory updates

PERF-02.justification: The recommendation engine is completely isolated from catalog browsing. User interaction events stream asynchronously via Amazon MSK, model inference uses cached feature vectors, and a Fallback Engine prevents browsing latency degradation during heavy recomputations.
sensitivity_points: Asynchronous decoupling of recommendation processing via MSK
tradeoffs: Serving heuristic fallback recommendations sacrifices personalization quality to preserve page latency

AVAIL-01.justification: Level 3 diagrams depict Order Management invoking Shipping & Fulfillment via synchronous in-process method calls which directly invoke Third-Party Shipping API over REST/HTTPS. An outage during checkout risks order failure without an explicit transactional outbox or asynchronous queue.
sensitivity_points: Synchronous coupling between checkout orchestration and external shipping API availability
Absence of fallback queuing mechanism in fulfillment component
tradeoffs: Synchronous fulfillment confirmation gives immediate tracking but degrades checkout resilience

AVAIL-02.justification: The system features multi-region active and failover readiness via Route 53 latency/health routing, CloudFront Origin Groups, Aurora Global Database cross-region storage replication (<1 s lag), and DynamoDB Global Tables to ensure high availability and zero lost orders.
sensitivity_points: Route 53 health check and DNS failover propagation time
tradeoffs: Cross-region data replication across multiple active regions incurs substantial operational costs

MOD-01.justification: Supporting a new currency requires changes across the Checkout & Billing component, external payment/tax integrations, and the frontend state management store, where supported currencies are explicitly enumerated. However, core data schemas and microservice boundaries remain unaffected.
sensitivity_points: Currency configuration encapsulation in client state and checkout services
tradeoffs: Delegating multi-currency conversions across external payment and tax services increases integration dependencies

MOD-02.justification: The Recommendation Engine is encapsulated in a standalone container exposing clean interfaces (FastAPI/gRPC). Algorithm changes are isolated to the Model Inference Worker and SageMaker Model Registry Client, requiring no modifications to external clients or services.
sensitivity_points: Strict adherence to API contract definitions between BFF and recommendation container
tradeoffs: Abstracting algorithm logic behind container boundaries introduces minor gRPC network overhead

SEC-01.justification: A comprehensive defense-in-depth posture defends against injection and XSS through AWS WAF on CloudFront and API Gateway, BFF Security & Compliance request sanitization interceptors, and Spring Data JPA parameterised queries in the repository layer.
sensitivity_points: WAF rule coverage and update cadence
Input sanitization rigor in BFF interceptor
tradeoffs: Multi-layer request payload inspection adds minimal processing latency to edge requests

SEC-02.justification: A specialized Compliance/Audit Lambda contains dedicated components for GDPR/CCPA Data Redactor, Compliance Policy Validator, and Report Generator. It directly redacts PII across Aurora and DynamoDB while producing verifiable audit trails in S3 and Athena.
sensitivity_points: Coverage of data discovery queries across Aurora, DynamoDB, and MSK logs
tradeoffs: Complete PII deletion and anonymization across global databases complicates relational referential integrity
